_about: Permission to reapply for admission after deportation or removal (Form I-212, src/reapply.py), per uscis.gov/i-212 (updated 06/01/2026, read 2026-10-02) and the I-212 instructions (edition 01/20/25, 'What Evidence Must You Submit?', pages 13-15): the G-28 and the I-212, then every document from each exclusion, deportation or removal proceeding, the family members' relationship and status, for INA 212(a)(9)(C) the evidence of 10 years outside the U.S., and the favorable factors (hardship, rehabilitation, family ties). With a Form I-601 in the same envelope the I-601's packet carries both (src/inadmissibility_waiver.py). The attorney approves titles and order.
title: Permission to reapply after removal (I-212)
requires_message: The client hasn't been processed yet: process the client first.

handwork.text: Copies of every document from each exclusion, deportation or removal proceeding, including the final order (the I-212 instructions, page 13).
The attorney's brief and the client's declaration: the favorable factors against the unfavorable, each with evidence behind it (the I-212 instructions, pages 14-15).

exhibits.title: Exclusion, deportation or removal proceedings: the orders and the notices
Family members in the U.S.: proof of U.S. citizenship or permanent residence, and of the relationship
For INA 212(a)(9)(C): evidence of 10 years outside the U.S. since the last departure (passport stamps, residence, work, bills)
Favorable factors: hardship to the family, rehabilitation, employment, community
Certified court dispositions and police records
USCIS notices and the visa case's letters
The client's passport and entry records

leave_out.intake_questionnaire: The firm's own intake questionnaire: internal.
leave_out.translation_certification: Goes with the document it translates.
leave_out.g28: The firm files a new G-28 with this application.
leave_out.work_permit: Not asked for with the I-212.
